chunks: My father and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with them - narrated, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr al-Bezanti, who said:
I read a letter from Abi al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) to Abi Ja'far (peace be upon him):

O Aba Ja'far! It has reached me that the servants, when you mount [your horse], take you out of the small door, and that is because of their stinginess, so that no one may benefit from you. So I ask you by my right upon you: let your entry and exit be only from the large door. And when you mount, let gold and silver be with you. Then, let no one ask you but that you give to him. From your paternal aunts, if they ask you to relieve their poverty, do not give them less than fifty dinars, and the abundant is up to you. And from your maternal aunts, do not give them less than twenty-five dinars, and the abundant is up to you. Indeed, I want only that Allah raises your rank. So spend, and do not fear from the Possessor of the Throne any decrease [in wealth].

key_terms.الْبَابِ الصَّغِيرِ: The small door (used for private or restricted exit)
key_terms.الْبَابِ الْكَبِيرِ: The large door (used for public access)

ai.seo_question: What are the instructions for social etiquette and financial generosity in the letter of Imam al-Rida to his son?
ai.summary: This letter from Imam al-Rida (AS) to his son Abi Ja'far emphasizes social visibility and strategic generosity as means of spiritual elevation, advising the use of the main gate to maximize public benefit. It prescribes specific minimum gifts for paternal and maternal relatives, grounded in the theological principle that spending in the way of God does not lead to loss, as affirmed by the promise 'do not fear deprivation from the Possessor of the Throne.'
